clue.text: Precise details of money and financial contributions, say

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: say signals that the following word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: taxes are contributions paid to the state; tax is the word said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone wants the exact figures on cash and tax payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you TAX is heard, not written: it sounds like TACKS. 'Getting down to brass tacks' means dealing with the basic facts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the basic, essential facts of a matter.

clue.text: Unnerves almost exposed poisoner

parts.note: rattles means unsettles or unnerves

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the word for exposed

parts.note: naked means bare or exposed

explanation.surface: A poisoner is nearly unmasked and loses their nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake poisons with its bite.

clue.text: Probe head's health

parts.note: to sound is to probe or test, as a depth or a person's views
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness place names

explanation.surface: A medical probe into a head teacher's state of health.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness is good condition, as in a sound body or mind.

clue.text: Watches people giving good marks

definitions.meaning: ticker is slang for a watch
people who mark work right with ticks

explanation.definitionFit: Tickers is slang for watches (and hearts), and literally those who put ticks on work.

clue.text: Swindle in secret component of contract

parts.note: a confidence is a secret told in trust
in contract bridge, the contract is a number of tricks to be won

explanation.surface: A fraud hidden in a clause of an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is the card game contract bridge, where a contract is made of tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A con trick wins a victim's trust in order to cheat them.

clue.text: Purpose of drama school is to bring boy up to read first

indicators.note: first says the word for read comes at the start

parts.note: to scan is to read through

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word for boy is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A drama school's aim is to raise a boy who reads early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drama school' is Sheridan's play The School for Scandal; scandal is what that school is for.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal names gossip and disgrace as its school's object.

clue.text: Flat in which I settled

indicators.note: in which says the second piece sits inside the first word, the flat

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat or apartment

explanation.surface: Describes the flat where the speaker made their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' looks like part of the story of the flat, but it is the definition: a bill settled is one paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill or debt that has been settled has been paid off.

clue.text: Stone forming a barrier

parts.note: a gate is a barrier across an opening

explanation.surface: A stone used to build a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a kind of chalcedony.

clue.text: Men enlisted for rough work

definitions.meaning: conscripted men, called up for service
a rough first version of a document

explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a group conscripted for service, and also a preliminary version of writing.

clue.text: Recusant needing conversion, one rather close to Rome?

indicators.note: a recusant refused to convert to the Church of England, and here the word's letters are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: A Catholic recusant who must convert, being someone near to Rome in faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing conversion' rearranges RECUSANT. 'Close to Rome' suggests Catholic loyalty, but the definition is geographic: the Etruscans lived just north of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were the people of Etruria, the region immediately neighbouring early Rome.

clue.text: A fighting force absorbing Spanish capital? Not half!

definitions.text: A fighting force absorbing Spanish capital? Not half!

indicators.note: absorbing means the force takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army unit

indicators.note: not half says only half the capital's name is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: Madrid is the capital of Spain

explanation.surface: A military body swallowing up Spain's money, with an emphatic exclamation at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' reads as British slang for 'very much'. The whole clue also describes the Spanish Armada of 1588, a fighting force paid for with Spanish money.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, famously the one Spain sent against England in 1588.

clue.text: Pawn in place that leads to small advantage

indicators.note: that leads to puts the first piece in front of the second

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
an edge is a slight advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: A chess pawn on a square that gives a slight positional plus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' looks like the chess piece, but it is the verb or noun of the pawnshop: something left as security.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pawned is handed over as security for a loan, which is a pledge.

clue.text: Not going straight — in court, desperate at heart

parts.note: a desperate situation is a dire one

explanation.surface: A criminal who refuses to go straight is in court, desperate inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not going straight' suggests a crook, but it simply means roundabout.
explanation.definitionFit: An indirect route is a roundabout one rather than a direct line.

clue.text: Touching alternative for girls lacking passes?

definitions.text: Touching alternative for girls lacking passes?

parts.words: Touching alternative for girls lacking passes?
parts.note: plays on the quip that men seldom make passes at girls who wear glasses; the alternative sits touching the eye

explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy Parker wrote 'Men seldom make passes / At girls who wear glasses'; this is what replaces the glasses, and it touches the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A small corrective disc worn on the eyeball replaces spectacles.

clue.text: Land in the sea — I almost get killed

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the word for killed

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay, to kill

explanation.surface: Someone fears being killed out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land surrounded by water; isle is the poetic form.

clue.text: Gripped a short while, then jump

parts.note: a spell is a short period of time
to bound is to leap or jump

explanation.surface: Someone held something briefly, then leapt.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spellbound is to be held fascinated, as if by magic.

clue.text: Noticing patient man losing head over maid, perhaps

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second
losing head removes the first letter of the patient man's name

parts.note: Job in the Bible is proverbial for patience
a maid is an example of a servant

explanation.surface: A patient man loses his head over a maid.
explanation.definitionFit: An observant person is quick to notice things.

clue.text: Mother joining husband in a particular European city

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: in puts the husband's letter inside the following phrase

parts.note: particular in the sense of fussy or exacting means strict

explanation.surface: A mother and her husband join up in some specific European city.
explanation.walkthrough: The H goes between the C and T of STRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Maastricht is a city in the south of the Netherlands, known for the 1992 EU treaty.

clue.text: Issue new shares in serious quantity

parts.note: real in the sense of genuine, not trivial, means serious
a lot is a quantity or batch

explanation.surface: A company issues more stock in large amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To reallot is to allocate again, as shares redistributed.

clue.text: Garment painter's finished with

definitions.meaning: the final layer a decorator applies

explanation.definitionFit: A topcoat is an overcoat, and the final layer of paint.

clue.text: Break in game

definitions.meaning: a simple card game where players call out on matching cards

explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a sudden break, and also the name of a children's card game.

clue.text: Impatient energy shown by workers in factory

indicators.note: in places the energy and workers inside the word for factory

parts.note: a plant is a factory or works
E is the physics symbol for energy
TU stands for trade union, a body of workers

explanation.surface: A factory's workers show irritable energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A petulant person is sulky and impatient, like a child who cannot wait.

clue.text: City in which couples get right above one

indicators.note: right, the letter R, is moved to stand before the letter I, which looks like one

parts.note: pairs are couples

explanation.surface: A romantic city where couples hope things come right.
explanation.walkthrough: In PAIRS, the R moves in front of the I (one), giving PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital of France.

clue.text: Fresh paint may be ostentatiously vulgar

definitions.meaning: wet paint is sticky to the touch

explanation.definitionFit: Tacky means slightly sticky, and also cheap and tasteless.

clue.text: You'll get angry when this criminal is executed

definitions.text: You'll get angry when this criminal is executed

parts.words: You'll get angry when this criminal is executed
parts.note: executing a criminal is read as cutting off the head, the first letter, and what remains is a word meaning angry; the criminal is a robber at sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' means beheaded: lose the P and IRATE (angry) is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a criminal who robs ships at sea.

clue.text: Go back after being fired

parts.note: describes what a gun does when it is discharged, kicking backwards

explanation.definitionFit: A firearm kicks backwards when discharged; the word also means to spring back or shrink away.

clue.text: Pagan procrastinator's confession

definitions.meaning: a pagan worships false gods or images
a procrastinator admits putting things off, in three words saying the task will be done at a later time

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as I DO LATER for the procrastinator.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, as a heathen or pagan does.

clue.text: Island sounding like heaven

indicators.note: sounding like says the word for heaven is heard, not written

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: An island whose name echoes the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a large Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides.

clue.text: Criticise what trains do for commuters

definitions.meaning: trains carry commuters to their jobs, read as bringing them to the task

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: trains take commuters to their work.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone to task is to reprimand them for a fault.
